title: Winners
summary: Links that keep winning go all the way strong. Losers go quiet.

cards.text:
If every win is a full step, and there is a ceiling,
winners march to the ceiling.

Losers march to the floor.
You are left with a few strong links, not a mush of medium ones.

question.prompt: After many wins and losses with hard ceilings, weights look like…
choices: a few at the ceiling, a few at the floor
question.why: Full-size steps plus walls empty the middle.
question.simpler: A step that shrinks as you near the wall stays mushier.

question.prompt: Without a wall, a link that only wins will grow without limit.
question.why: The wall is what stops the march.
question.simpler: An additive win has no natural stopping point.

recall.question: Do additive wins with a ceiling leave weights spread evenly?
recall.answer: No. They pile up at the ceiling and the floor.

deeper.note: Song, Miller, and Abbott showed the competition. The histogram going to two piles is the result.

paper.title: Competitive Hebbian learning through spike-timing-dependent synaptic plasticity
paper.section: The model and the bimodal weights.

terms.plain: a few links at the ceiling
terms.definition: When additive STDP plus hard bounds drives weights to the extremes, so a neuron selects a subset of inputs.
